newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo civilians face extra night in strife-hit city.
newsitem.headline: Congo civilians face extra night in strife-hit city.

text.p: French armed forces evacuating civilians from the strife-ridden Congolese capital hoped to fly a further 200 out before nightfall on Wednesday, a military spokesman said.

But with exchanges of fire coming as close as 50 metres (yards) from the airport building where they were sheltering, the spokesman said it had been decided to ferry more than 200 others, for whom there was no hope of evacuation on Wednesday, back to safe sites in the city.

He said the civilians, of various nationalities but including only a few French nationals, most of whom have already been flown to safety, would be transported in buses and cars under heavy armed escort.
"We are not abandoning you, we are going to get the maximum number of people out of here. Those who have to go into town -- it is for your own security," a French officer assured the civilians.
But as stray bullets hit the compound, forcing the civilians, women and children among them, to lie on the ground for safety, the announcement met a reluctant response.
"I want to get out of this place -- it is a dangerous place and we don't feel well-protected here," Lebanese George Bakhri told Reuters.
"But we don't want to go back into Brazzaville, it is much too dangerous and we fear for our lives,"

The firing around the airport was mainly from small arms, with only an occasional mortar and rocket-propelled grenade round. A 10-year-old boy was hit in the hand by a stray bullet, but there were no other casualties among the civilians.

Witnesses said the level of firing in the city itself was lower than in previous days, following a unilateral ceasefire called by President Pascal Lissouba, which has been at least partially observed by his own men.
